questions.stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to AUSPICIOUS.
questions.explanation: B is correct. AUSPICIOUS = promising success; favourable. INAUSPICIOUS = not showing signs of future success; unfavourable, ill-omened. Synonyms of auspicious: propitious, favourable, promising.

questions.stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to DILIGENT.
questions.explanation: C is correct. DILIGENT = having or showing care and conscientiousness in one's work. Its antonym is LAZY = unwilling to work. Other antonyms: indolent, slothful, negligent.

questions.stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to GENEROUS.
questions.explanation: D is correct. GENEROUS = giving or sharing willingly. MISERLY = spending as little as possible; mean with money. Other antonyms: stingy, parsimonious, niggardly, tightfisted.

questions.stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to VERBOSE.
questions.explanation: A is correct. VERBOSE = using more words than needed; wordy. TERSE = brief and to the point. Synonyms of verbose: wordy, loquacious, prolix, long-winded. Antonyms: terse, laconic, succinct, concise.

questions.stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to PENITENT.
questions.explanation: B is correct. PENITENT = feeling or showing sorrow and regret for having done wrong; repentant. UNREPENTANT = showing no regret for one's wrongdoing. Synonym of penitent: contrite. Antonyms: unrepentant, impenitent, shameless.

questions.stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to GREGARIOUS.
questions.explanation: C is correct. GREGARIOUS = fond of company; sociable. RECLUSIVE = avoiding the company of other people; solitary. Other antonyms: introverted, antisocial, withdrawn, hermitic.

questions.stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to BENIGN.
questions.explanation: C is correct. BENIGN = gentle and kind; not harmful (especially in medical context: benign tumour). MALIGNANT = very virulent or infectious; harmful; (medical) cancerous and life-threatening. The contrast is stark in medicine: benign vs. malignant tumour.

questions.stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to LAUD.
questions.explanation: D is correct. LAUD = to praise highly (from Latin laudare = to praise). CONDEMN = to express strong disapproval of. Synonyms of laud: extol, exalt, acclaim, commend. Antonyms: censure, condemn, castigate, lambaste.

questions.stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to PERFIDIOUS.
questions.explanation: A is correct. PERFIDIOUS = deceitful and untrustworthy; guilty of betrayal (from Latin: per = to ruin + fides = faith). LOYAL = giving or showing firm and constant support. Antonyms: faithful, trustworthy, loyal, steadfast. Synonyms: treacherous, disloyal, faithless, duplicitous.

questions.stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to SANGUINE.
questions.explanation: D is correct. SANGUINE = optimistic, especially in a difficult situation. DESPONDENT = in low spirits from loss of hope or courage; pessimistic. Note: 'sanguine' originally referred to the ruddy complexion of blood (Latin: sanguis = blood) associated with a cheerful temperament. Antonyms: despondent, pessimistic, gloomy, melancholic.
